dedupe_keys.name: tsunami runup survey data from the taan fjord landslide event

description: Tsunami Runup Survey Data From The Taan Fjord Landslide Event is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Patrick J. Lynett et al. On 17 October 2015, a mountainside collapse at the terminus of Tyndall Glacier in southeast Alaska generated a landslide-triggered mega-tsunami. The landslide sent approximately 7.6 × 107 m3 of rock and glacial sediment into Taan Fjord, abruptly displacing the water. Coverage: not stated; published in 2025. Formats: Excel, MATLAB, Image, KML. The data are held in Designsafe-CI and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
